# Robustness: the naive--uncertainty contrast across estimators {#sec-app-robust}

The main text estimates regime instability as a discrete-time hazard of a change in the Regimes of the World classification, and reports that the apparently significant effects of public opinion under point-estimate estimation dissolve once measurement uncertainty is propagated.
Here we show that this contrast is not an artifact of that particular operationalization.
@tbl-robust reproduces the two focal quantities---the discontent-by-support interaction and the discontent main effect---estimated both ways, under five operationalizations of regime instability: the main Regimes-of-the-World discrete-time hazard; the narrower discrete-time hazard defined by V-Dem's Episodes of Regime Transformation transition variable [@Maerz2024]; a Cox proportional-hazards survival model in which regime spells are the unit of risk and the baseline hazard is left unparameterized; the Geddes-Wright-Frantz binary indicator of autocratic regime breakdown [@Geddes2014]; and Powell and Thyne's coup events [@Powell2011].

The pattern in the three transition-based specifications is identical.
Among autocracies, the discontent-by-support interaction is positive and statistically significant under point estimates in every one (coefficients of 0.25 to 0.27, all $p < 0.05$), and in every one it loses significance once the uncertainty of the latent measures is propagated by the method of composition ($p$ between 0.15 and 0.23).
The two remaining measures are supplementary, because their risk sets shrink drastically in the survey era: only 11 Geddes-Wright-Frantz breakdowns and 20 coup attempts fall within the estimation sample, reflecting the fact that breakdown- and coup-prone countries are precisely those least covered by cross-national surveys.
Within that limit they tell the same story: the discontent coefficient in the breakdown model is marginally significant under point estimates ($p = 0.096$) and attenuates to insignificance under the method of composition ($p = 0.15$), and no opinion term approaches significance in any coup model under either estimator.
That five operationalizations built on different outcome definitions and different treatments of duration all reproduce the same naive-to-null reversal---or show no effect to begin with---indicates that the finding is a general property of taking measurement uncertainty seriously, not a feature of any single modeling choice.

The conclusion is equally insensitive to specification of the hazard itself.
Adding period dummies to the main model---motivated by the temporal clustering of regime change, and warranted: the post-2010 period raises the hazard of democratic deterioration substantially (log-odds $1.95$, $p = 0.005$), the backsliding wave---leaves every focal estimate essentially unchanged, and in fact weakens even the naive autocratic interaction (from $p = 0.050$ to $p = 0.064$).
Replacing the logged regime-tenure term with a cubic polynomial in regime age likewise changes nothing of substance.
Neither period effects nor the parameterization of duration dependence, then, accounts for the results.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-robust
#| tbl-cap: "Focal coefficients under point-estimate vs. uncertainty-propagated estimation, across five operationalizations of regime instability"

p_load(kableExtra)
source(here::here("data", "customFunctions.R"))
hz  <- readRDS(here::here("results_regime_hazard_full.rds"))
pt  <- readRDS(here::here("results_hazard_pointest.rds"))
er  <- readRDS(here::here("results_ert_interaction.rds"))
cx  <- readRDS(here::here("results_regime_survival.rds"))
rn  <- readRDS(here::here("results_robust_naive.rds"))
gwf <- readRDS(here::here("results_gwf_robust.rds"))
cp  <- readRDS(here::here("results_coup_robust.rds"))

stars <- function(p) ifelse(p < .01, "***", ifelse(p < .05, "**", ifelse(p < .1, "*", "")))
cell  <- function(e, s, p) sprintf("%.3f%s (%.3f)", e, stars(p), s)
moc_get <- function(m, tm) {   # m = data.frame of MOC draws
  s <- suppressWarnings(MOCsumm(m)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(e = as.numeric(estimate), se = as.numeric(std.error), p = 2*(1-pnorm(abs(e/se)))) |>
    dplyr::filter(term == tm); cell(s$e, s$se, s$p)
}
nv_get <- function(d, tm) {
  d <- tibble::as_tibble(d)
  s <- dplyr::mutate(d, p = if ("p" %in% names(d)) p else 2*(1-pnorm(abs(est/se)))) |> dplyr::filter(term == tm)
  cell(s$est, s$se, s$p)
}

rows <- tibble::tribble(
  ~spec, ~regime, ~events, ~naive, ~moc,
  "RoW change (discrete-time)", "Democracies", hz[["DETERIORATION [dem] (Firth)"]]$n_ev,
      pt[["DETERIOR [dem] Firth"]], hz[["DETERIORATION [dem] (Firth)"]]$coef,
  "RoW change (discrete-time)", "Autocracies", hz[["IMPROVEMENT [aut] (Firth)"]]$n_ev,
      pt[["IMPROVE [aut] Firth"]],  hz[["IMPROVEMENT [aut] (Firth)"]]$coef,
  "ERT reg\\_trans (discrete-time)", "Democracies", er[["break_dem"]]$n_ev,
      rn[["regtrans breakdown [dem]"]],  er[["break_dem"]]$coef,
  "ERT reg\\_trans (discrete-time)", "Autocracies", er[["trans_aut"]]$n_ev,
      rn[["regtrans transition [aut]"]], er[["trans_aut"]]$coef,
  "Cox proportional hazards", "Democracies", cx[["democracies"]]$n_fail,
      rn[["cox breakdown [dem]"]],       cx[["democracies"]]$coef,
  "Cox proportional hazards", "Autocracies", cx[["autocracies"]]$n_fail,
      rn[["cox democratization [aut]"]], cx[["autocracies"]]$coef,
  "GWF autocratic breakdown", "Autocracies", gwf$n_ev,
      gwf$naive, gwf$moc,
  "Powell--Thyne coup attempts", "All regimes", cp[["attempt [all] moc"]]$n_ev,
      cp[["attempt [all] naive"]], cp[["attempt [all] moc"]]$coef,
  "Powell--Thyne coup attempts", "Autocracies", cp[["attempt [aut] moc"]]$n_ev,
      cp[["attempt [aut] naive"]], cp[["attempt [aut] moc"]]$coef
)
out <- rows |> dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(int_n = nv_get(naive, "disc_supp"), int_m = moc_get(moc, "disc_supp"),
                dis_n = nv_get(naive, "disc_c"),     dis_m = moc_get(moc, "disc_c")) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

tab <- out |> dplyr::select(regime, events, int_n, int_m, dis_n, dis_m)
colnames(tab) <- c(" ", "Events", "Point est.", "Uncertainty", "Point est.", "Uncertainty")

kbl(tab, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, align = c("l", "c", rep("c", 4)), linesep = "") |>
  add_header_above(c(" " = 2, "Discontent $\\\\times$ Support" = 2, "Political discontent" = 2), escape = FALSE) |>
  pack_rows(index = table(factor(out$spec, levels = unique(out$spec)))) |>
  kable_styling(font_size = 9, latex_options = c("hold_position", "scale_down")) |>
  footnote(general_title = "", threeparttable = TRUE, escape = FALSE,
    general = paste0("Log-odds (discrete-time hazard) or log-hazard (Cox) coefficients with ",
      "standard errors in parentheses. `Point est.' plugs in posterior means of the latent ",
      "measures; `Uncertainty' propagates their measurement uncertainty across 900 draws by the ",
      "method of composition. Discrete-time democracy/autocracy and GWF/coup models use Firth ",
      "penalized likelihood with model-based standard errors (the pooled coup model uses ",
      "country-clustered logit); Cox and non-penalized logit models use country-clustered ",
      "standard errors and yield the same pattern. GWF coverage ends in 2010; the GWF and coup ",
      "rows are supplementary given their small event counts in the survey era. ",
      "*** p<0.01, ** p<0.05, * p<0.1."))
```
